title: Macroscopic Structural and Connectome Mapping of the Mouse Brain Using Diffusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging
author: Tanzil Mahmud Arefin

steps.title: Prepare materials and reagents
steps.instruction: Gather the following items: 5 ml syringe (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat Z683582‑100EA); Vacutainer safety‑lock blood collection set (25 G × 3/4″ × 12″, 0.5 × 19 × 305 mm, Becton Dickinson, cat 367283); nylon zip‑ties (4″ and 8″, LECO plastics, part L‑4‑18, L‑8‑50); 50 ml conical tubes (Corning, cat 352070); BALB/cByJ mice (Jackson Labs, cat 001026, 8‑10 weeks old, both sexes); chloral hydrate (Sigma, cat 102425); heparin (Sigma, cat H3393‑50KU); PBS (Corning, cat 21‑031); gadodiamide (Omniscan, CAS 131410‑48‑5); 10 % formalin solution (PolyScience, cat 08279‑20); perfluoropolyether (Fomblin®, PerkinElmer, CAS 69991067‑9, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat 317926).

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Inject chloral hydrate intraperitoneally at 100 mg kg⁻¹ dissolved in sterile PBS.

steps.title: Transcardial perfusion with PBS/heparin then formalin
steps.instruction: Perfuse the mouse transcardially with 35 ml cold PBS containing heparin at 50 units ml⁻¹, followed immediately by 35 ml 10 % formalin; maintain a flow rate of ~12 ml min⁻¹ for each solution and confirm successful perfusion by the liver turning from dark red to brown‑grey and the carcass becoming stiff.

steps.title: Post‑fix head in formalin
steps.instruction: Decapitate at the mid‑cervical line (≈C3‑C4) without damaging the spinal cord, place the head in 50 ml 10 % formalin at 4 °C for 24 h in a 50 ml conical tube.

steps.title: Replace formalin with PBS and store
steps.instruction: After the 24 h fixation, discard the formalin, add PBS to the tube, and keep the sample at 4 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Incubate in gadodiamide solution
steps.instruction: Replace the PBS with 50 ml of 2 mM gadodiamide dissolved in PBS; store at 4 °C for one week to allow diffusion of the contrast agent into the tissue.

steps.title: Trim external tissues and remove mandible
steps.instruction: Trim away skin and muscle while preserving the skull and eyeballs; then remove the mandible bone and the tongue.

steps.title: Mount brain in syringe with zip‑ties
steps.instruction: Place the brain in the barrel of a 5 ml syringe with the nose pointing toward the hub; insert 2–3 small bent pieces of zip‑tie at the bottom and back of the brain to secure it.

steps.title: Fill syringe with Fomblin and degas
steps.instruction: Replace the syringe cap with a loosely tied Vacutainer, fill the barrel with perfluoropolyether (Fomblin®), insert the plunger, flip the syringe so the hub points upward, and remove the cap.

steps.title: Vacuum‑remove air bubbles
steps.instruction: Place the upright syringe in a vacuum chamber for 30 min to eliminate trapped air bubbles.

steps.title: Seal syringe and remove residual air
steps.instruction: After vacuum treatment, remove the syringe, push out any remaining air and PBS from the barrel, and tighten the Vacutainer to seal the cap securely.

steps.title: Place syringe in cryogenic holder
steps.instruction: Lay the syringe horizontally in the animal holder designed for the cryogenic probe; adjust the position so the dorsal brain surface is as close as possible to the cryogenic coil and tape the syringe to the holder.

steps.title: Insert holder into MRI magnet
steps.instruction: Insert the holder (with syringe) into the magnet bore beneath the cryogenic probe.

steps.title: Run Localizer pilot scan and verify position
steps.instruction: Acquire a pilot scan using the Bruker Localizer protocol; examine the three orthogonal reference images to confirm the specimen lies in the most sensitive region of the cryogenic coil with no left/right tilt; if necessary, reposition the sample and repeat the Localizer scan.

steps.title: Shim magnetic field using MapShim
steps.instruction: Adjust the tuning and matching of the cryogenic probe, then acquire a B₀ field map; open the Bruker MapShim dialog, select the appropriate scan, choose Map_shim, define a target volume (cubic, cylindrical, or ellipsoidal) that fully encloses the brain, adjust its size/position/rotation, run the shim calculation, and apply the resulting shim currents to achieve a homogeneous B₀ field.

steps.title: Acquire HARDI diffusion MRI with specified parameters
steps.instruction: Perform high‑angular‑resolution diffusion‑weighted imaging (HARDI) using a modified 3D GRASE sequence (or alternatively a 3D multi‑shot diffusion‑weighted EPI sequence) with the following settings: TE/TR = 33/400 min, 2 non‑diffusion‑weighted (b₀) images, 60 diffusion‑weighted images auto‑generated, b‑value = 5 000 s mm⁻², isotropic resolution = 100 µm.
